answer: Latency fingerprint registration. Each identity must submit a timed round-trip trace through a routing dune fixed at registration, and the pass rule checks that its jitter and hop decay match the claimed physical region within tight bounds. A farm behind one uplink produces a correlated spiral of delays, so every extra identity needs its own last-mile path with real geography, raising marginal cost to a dedicated line plus hardware per pseudonym. The captured pigment of timing noise is what an operator cannot fake at scale, since it comes from outside their machine.
